title: Align TaskStop tool with the TS baseline
objective: Implement all TaskStop improvements identified by the per-tool subagent report so the Go clone matches the original TypeScript tool in public contract, runtime logic, robustness, state lifecycle, and tests.

context.problem: TaskStop is partially aligned on the happy-path input names and success JSON fields, but it is not yet fully equivalent to the TS baseline. The main gaps are legacy KillShell lookup, SDK stop_task support, TS-style validation/error typing, broader task-runtime dispatch, stopped-task lifecycle side effects, persisted-running-task handling, and typed output/UI metadata parity.

parallelization_notes: Can be assigned to an implementation subagent after listed dependencies are available. Avoid running concurrently with another task that owns the same files.

improvement_points.title: Legacy KillShell alias is not registered for TaskStop
improvement_points.description: TS publishes TaskStop with aliases:['KillShell'] and both validateInput/call accept the deprecated shell_id parameter for KillShell compatibility. Go's registry can resolve aliases only when a tool implements Aliases(), but TaskStopTool only exposes Name/Description/Schema/Execute and therefore registry.Get("KillShell") will not find it. The only Go KillShell normalization found is inside agent profile/tool-name parsing, not the top-level tool registry.

improvement_points.title: SDK stop_task control request is missing
improvement_points.description: TS explicitly shares stopTask between the LLM tool and SDK stop_task control requests. Go's SDK transport routes initialize, interrupt, set_model, set_permission_mode, set_max_thinking_tokens, resume, compact, and get_context_usage, but has no stop_task case, no StopTaskRequest type, and no Engine method that exposes the BackgroundTaskManager stop operation to the SDK layer.

improvement_points.title: Validation and error typing do not match TS
improvement_points.description: TS uses a strict input object, validates missing/not-found/not-running before call execution, returns validation errorCode 1 or 3, and stopTask throws StopTaskError with machine-readable codes not_found, not_running, and unsupported_type. Go parses through json.Unmarshal, silently ignores unknown fields, trims task_id/shell_id whitespace before deciding missing, returns only ToolResult.IsError with a plain message, and adds a Go-only persisted-running-in-another-process error without a typed code.

improvement_points.title: Stop dispatch covers only Go background-manager task types
improvement_points.description: TS dispatches stop through getTaskByType over a broader runtime task registry: local_bash, local_agent, remote_agent, dream, and feature-gated local_workflow/monitor_mcp implementations. If a visible running task has no registered implementation, TS reports unsupported_type. Go's BackgroundTaskManager defines only local_bash and local_agent constants, TaskStop directly calls Background.Stop, and Stop has no type-specific kill registry or unsupported_type branch for other runtime task records.

improvement_points.title: Stopped-task lifecycle side effects are not TS-equivalent
improvement_points.description: TS does more than cancel: local shell stops mark notified=true to suppress the noisy killed notification and emit a task_terminated SDK event directly; remote-agent stops mark notified, emit SDK termination, archive the remote session, evict output, and remove metadata; dream stops mark notified and roll back the consolidation lock. Go Stop sets status=killed/exit=-1/finished_at, cancels/kills, persists the record, and later emits a generic Notification hook from the background goroutine. RuntimeTaskRecord has Notified and OutputOffset fields, but BackgroundTask.recordLocked never populates Notified and BackgroundTask has no notified state.

improvement_points.title: Persisted running tasks can be visible but cannot be stopped or restored
improvement_points.description: TS validates against the current appState task map and any visible running task is expected to have an in-process task implementation that can be killed. Go TaskOutput/Snapshot can surface persisted runtime records from .claude/runtime-tasks, including running records, but BackgroundTaskManager.Stop refuses a running persisted record that is not in this manager with 'running in another process and cannot be stopped from this session'. The stored-agent restore path likewise refuses running records from another process.

improvement_points.title: Typed output schema and UI/tool metadata parity are incomplete
improvement_points.description: TS declares an output schema with message, task_id, task_type, and optional command, sets maxResultSizeChars=100000, shouldDefer, searchHint, userFacingName, concurrency safety, toAutoClassifierInput, custom prompt text, empty tool-use rendering, and a truncated UI result renderer. Go returns equivalent success fields as a JSON string via ResponseJSON and has registry-level deferred metadata, but the Tool interface/result type has no output schema, max-result metadata, user-facing name, classifier projection, concurrency-safety metadata, or TaskStop-specific render/prompt surface.

improvement_points.title: Go regression coverage is narrow for TaskStop parity
improvement_points.description: Existing Go tests cover a shell happy path, cleanup after a TaskOutput timeout, and local-agent killed metadata persistence. They do not lock the TS-specific legacy alias, shell_id path, missing/not-found/not-running/unsupported-type errors, strict input behavior, SDK stop_task control request, notification/notified side effects, or persisted-running-task behavior.

implementation_subtasks.title: Register TaskStop's KillShell alias
implementation_steps: Add an Aliases() []string method to TaskStopTool returning []string{"KillShell"}.
Keep shell_id input compatibility unchanged.
Add registry tests proving registry.Get("KillShell") returns the TaskStop tool and ExecuteTool can stop using shell_id.
Confirm agent-profile legacy normalization still maps KillShell to TaskStop without becoming the only alias path.
acceptance_criteria: TaskStopTool implements types.AliasedTool.
A registry containing TaskStop resolves both TaskStop and KillShell to the same tool.
KillShell invoked with shell_id stops a running background task and returns the same success JSON fields as TaskStop with task_id.
risks: Alias registration must not add KillShell to model-facing tool definitions; it should remain lookup-only like other Go aliases.
non_goals: Do not reintroduce a separate KillShell implementation.
Do not change TaskOutput legacy aliases in this task.

implementation_subtasks.title: Wire SDK stop_task to the same stop runtime as TaskStop
implementation_steps: Add StopTaskRequest with subtype stop_task and task_id.
Extend SDKServer.handleControlRequest with a stop_task case.
Expose a narrow engine-level StopTask method or optional internal interface that calls the configured BackgroundTaskManager/stop runtime.
Return control_response success with an empty response payload on success, matching TS.
Return control_response error using the stop error message on failure.
Add SDK transport tests for success, not-found, malformed request, and unsupported stop runtime.
acceptance_criteria: SDK control_request {subtype:'stop_task', task_id:'...'} stops a running Go background task.
The successful control_response has subtype success and no extra payload, matching TS print.ts behavior.
Not-found/not-running failures return control_response subtype error with the stop message.
Existing interrupt/set_model/resume/compact control tests still pass.
risks: Engine currently stores BackgroundTasks behind a compact read-only interface; keep the new stop capability narrow and optional instead of widening unrelated compact APIs.
non_goals: Do not change the SDK permission-response protocol.
Do not make SDK stop_task stop arbitrary OS processes outside the runtime task manager.

implementation_subtasks.title: Add TS-compatible TaskStop validation and typed stop errors
implementation_steps: Introduce a small StopTaskError type with Code values not_found, not_running, unsupported_type, and a separate code/path for Go-only cross-process refusal if kept.
Have BackgroundTaskManager.Stop return StopTaskError for not found and not running instead of generic fmt.Errorf.
Add TaskStop input validation that rejects missing task_id/shell_id with the TS message and preserves the TS precedence task_id ?? shell_id.
Decide deliberately whether to keep or remove Go's strings.TrimSpace behavior; exact TS parity treats whitespace-only ids as ids, not missing input.
Represent strict input semantics for TaskStop where the Go schema/parser can express it, including rejecting unknown fields if a strict parser is available.
Add tests for missing input, shell_id fallback, task_id precedence over shell_id, not-found, not-running, non-string input, and unknown fields.
acceptance_criteria: Missing task id returns 'Missing required parameter: task_id'.
Not found returns 'No task found with ID: <id>' and a machine-readable not_found code internally.
Not running returns 'Task <id> is not running (status: <status>)' and a machine-readable not_running code internally.
Unsupported task type is distinguishable from not found/not running.
TaskStop behavior for task_id plus shell_id matches TS precedence.
risks: A global strict parse change could affect many tools; prefer TaskStop-local validation unless a shared strict-parser migration is already planned.
non_goals: Do not change TaskCreate/TaskGet/TaskUpdate input parsing in this task.
Do not redesign ToolResult error transport beyond what TaskStop needs.

implementation_subtasks.title: Introduce a task-type-aware stop dispatcher
dependencies: Add TS-compatible TaskStop validation and typed stop errors
implementation_steps: Define a small internal stop handler interface keyed by runtime task type.
Register handlers for local_bash and local_agent using existing BackgroundTaskManager cancellation paths.
Return unsupported_type for visible running records whose type has no registered stop handler.
Preserve current child-task cascade behavior for local_agent/local_bash where it is a Go runtime requirement.
Add tests with synthetic runtime records/tasks for supported local_bash/local_agent and unsupported type values.
acceptance_criteria: TaskStop routes local_bash and local_agent through explicit type handlers.
A running task with an unregistered type returns unsupported_type instead of a generic missing/cross-process error when it is visible to the runtime.
Adding a future remote_agent/dream handler does not require changing TaskStopTool.Execute.
Existing shell and agent stop tests still pass.
risks: Some Go task types may not yet exist; keep unsupported handling explicit rather than pretending to implement TS remote/dream behavior prematurely.
non_goals: Do not implement remote_agent cloud APIs or dream memory consolidation unless those runtimes already exist in Go.
Do not remove Go's child cascade unless a separate parity decision approves it.

implementation_subtasks.title: Align stopped-task lifecycle notifications and cleanup
implementation_steps: Add notified state to BackgroundTask or otherwise persist RuntimeTaskRecord.Notified from the stop path.
For local_bash TaskStop, mark notified before the completion goroutine emits a killed notification so the Go runtime can suppress duplicate/noisy model notifications.
Add or reuse an SDK task-terminated event helper for stopped tasks if the Go SDK event layer supports task lifecycle events.
Keep generic completion hooks for natural completed/failed tasks, but gate stopped-task hooks to match TS notification semantics.
Add type-specific cleanup hooks for any Go runtimes equivalent to TS remote_agent or dream when those handlers exist.
Add tests proving local shell stopped by TaskStop is persisted notified/killed and does not emit a duplicate completion notification.
acceptance_criteria: Stopped local_bash records persist status killed, exit -1, finished_at, and notified=true or equivalent suppression state.
Stopping a local_bash task does not enqueue/emit a redundant generic killed model notification.
SDK lifecycle listeners receive a stopped/terminated event for stopped tasks when the Go SDK task lifecycle channel is enabled.
Natural completed/failed task notifications continue to fire once.
risks: Notification behavior may be shared with hooks; tests should isolate hook emission so suppressing TaskStop noise does not hide real completed/failed events.
non_goals: Do not redesign the whole hook system.
Do not add remote-agent archive calls unless a Go remote-agent runtime is present.

implementation_subtasks.title: Resolve persisted-running-task stop semantics
dependencies: Add TS-compatible TaskStop validation and typed stop errors
implementation_steps: Define the intended Go equivalent of TS 'visible task is stoppable': reattach, mark stale, or hide from TaskOutput.
If reattaching local_agent records is feasible, restore enough session state to cancel the task or mark it no longer running before exposing it.
If cross-process stopping is impossible, classify persisted running records as stale/unavailable consistently in TaskOutput and TaskStop instead of advertising them as live not_ready tasks.
Add tests for a running record present only in RuntimeTaskStore: TaskOutput behavior and TaskStop behavior must agree.
Ensure completed/failed persisted records remain readable by TaskOutput.
acceptance_criteria: A task shown by TaskOutput as running/not_ready is stoppable by TaskStop in the same process.
A running record from another process is either reattached and stoppable or classified as stale/unavailable in both TaskOutput and TaskStop.
Completed/failed persisted records are still retrievable for output inspection.
The user-facing error text for truly cross-process tasks is tested and typed, not a generic fmt.Errorf branch.
risks: Cross-process process killing is OS- and ownership-sensitive; prefer a conservative stale/unavailable classification if safe reattachment is not available.
non_goals: Do not kill arbitrary PIDs read from disk without ownership/session validation.
Do not change completed-task output retention policy.

implementation_subtasks.title: Expose TaskStop output schema and metadata parity hooks
implementation_steps: Add optional tool metadata interfaces for output schema, max result size, user-facing name, classifier input, concurrency safety, and prompt text where the Go runtime consumes them.
Implement the relevant metadata on TaskStopTool.
Keep the current success JSON keys message, task_id, task_type, and command.
If UI rendering exists for Go tool results, add the TS-equivalent stopped command rendering and truncation behavior.
Add tests for metadata discovery and stable success payload fields.
acceptance_criteria: TaskStop publishes an output schema equivalent to TS's message/task_id/task_type/command shape.
TaskStop metadata includes should-defer/search hint, max result size, concurrency-safe, and classifier projection where supported.
Visible success payload remains JSON with the four TS fields.
Any Go UI renderer shows '<command> · stopped' with TS-equivalent truncation when not verbose.
risks: Adding metadata interfaces can affect many tools; keep them optional and verify zero-value behavior for existing tools.
non_goals: Do not change TaskStop runtime cancellation semantics in this metadata task.
Do not add UI-only metadata to API tool definitions unless the TS API also exposes it.

implementation_subtasks.title: Build a TaskStop parity regression suite
dependencies: Wire SDK stop_task to the same stop runtime as TaskStop
Add TS-compatible TaskStop validation and typed stop errors
Align stopped-task lifecycle notifications and cleanup
implementation_steps: Add table-driven TaskStop input/error tests for missing, shell_id, task_id precedence, not found, not running, unsupported type, and unknown/non-string fields.
Add registry alias tests for KillShell.
Add lifecycle tests for stopped shell and agent tasks, including persisted status, exit code, finished_at, and notification suppression/SDK closeout where implemented.
Add SDK stop_task success and failure tests.
Add persisted-running-record tests that assert TaskOutput and TaskStop agree on visibility/stoppability.
acceptance_criteria: Each TS compatibility branch identified in this report has at least one Go regression test.
The suite fails if KillShell alias support is removed.
The suite fails if SDK stop_task returns unsupported subtype.
The suite fails if TaskStop cannot distinguish missing/not-found/not-running/unsupported-type.
The suite documents any intentional Go-only cross-process behavior with explicit assertions.
risks: Some tests depend on implementation tasks above. If added before implementation, mark only those future-facing cases with precise t.Skip messages tied to this report's gap ids.
non_goals: Do not create broad flaky integration tests that spawn long-lived external processes.
Do not update production code in this test-suite task except minimal test hooks needed for deterministic assertions.
